content.value_statement: Agent systems often fail because context is too large, stale, or poorly organized. This skill teaches practical context design, budgeting, and progressive disclosure patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents, message history, and tool outputs.
Describes context windows, attention limits, and context degradation effects.
Shows how progressive disclosure keeps agent context focused and efficient.
Provides guidance for context budgeting, compaction, and placement of critical information.
Includes example utilities for token estimation, context building, and message truncation.
limitations: It is educational guidance, not a complete agent framework.
Token counts are approximate and should not replace provider-specific tokenizers.
It does not include live model benchmarks or vendor-specific context limits.
It does not automatically optimize existing production systems.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Context
use_cases.description: Plan which instructions, tools, documents, and message history belong in an agent runtime.

use_cases.title: Debug Context Failures
use_cases.description: Trace failures caused by missing information, overloaded context, stale retrieval, or poor placement.

use_cases.title: Teach Context Basics
use_cases.description: Onboard team members to context windows, progressive disclosure, and token budgeting concepts before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main components of context in an agent system. Use simple language and connect each component to one design decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Prompt Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this system prompt outline: [paste outline]. Identify missing sections, unclear instructions, and context that should load later.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Progressive Disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a progressive disclosure plan for this agent: [describe agent]. Specify what to preload, what to retrieve on demand, and why.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Context Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this agent architecture for context risk: [describe architecture]. Cover attention limits, tool outputs, message history, compaction, and degradation handling.

output_examples.input: I am building a support agent with many policy documents.
output_examples.output: Preload the core policy summary, retrieve detailed policies only when needed, and summarize long customer histories after fixed thresholds.

output_examples.input: Our coding agent performs worse in long debugging sessions.
output_examples.output: Likely causes include noisy tool outputs, stale assumptions in message history, and important constraints buried in the middle of context.

output_examples.input: I need to teach a team why context size matters.
output_examples.output: Use the attention budget explanation, then compare exhaustive loading with a smaller progressive disclosure workflow.

best_practices: Start with the smallest high-signal context that supports the current task.
Keep critical instructions near the beginning or end of the context.
Use summaries and compaction thresholds before long histories overwhelm the model.
anti_patterns: Preloading every document before the task is known.
Treating long context windows as a replacement for careful curation.
Ignoring tool output size after each agent action.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches how agent context is structured, constrained, loaded, and managed during AI workflows.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The concepts apply to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other agent systems.

faq.question: Does it run tools or commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example utilities. It does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it replace retrieval design?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan retrieval, but it does not implement a full retrieval system.

faq.question: Does it provide exact token counts?
faq.answer: No. It includes approximate estimates and recommends provider-specific tokenizers for production systems.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: AI engineers, prompt engineers, and technical leads can use it to design more reliable agent context.
